tb21_profile.skill: Build a C project from a vendored source tarball with non-default compiler/configure flags (gcov instrumentation) and install the binary so it resolves on PATH
tb21_profile.domain: Linux toolchain: autotools/make, gcc coverage instrumentation (.gcno/.gcda), SQLite source distribution, Ubuntu apt build deps
tb21_profile.task_form: build/packaging + environment configuration from source; few steps but must get the flag plumbing and install location right

searches: tools.py words all compile "from source" PATH install make -n 30
tools.py words tw compile build "from source" tarball install system-wide -n 30

Vendored SQLite source whose build config disables features; must repair config and compile sqlite3 with features on.

Repair missing linker flag in SQLite amalgamation Makefile and build sqlite3 binary; identical compile/link-flag debugging.
Fix Makefile.in, ./configure --prefix=/usr/local, make install so the built binary is on PATH and usable downstream.
Vendored zlib: repair build system, configure --prefix, make install, then link against the install prefix.
Vendored jq-1.6 tarball with injected build regression; diagnose ./configure && make failure and get a working binary.
Autotools chain end-to-end: chmod configure, fix Makefile.am, autoreconf -i, configure, make for vendored fping.
libseccomp configure carries an invalid hardcoded compiler flag; find it, build and install to a local prefix.
Fix broken Makefile for vendored sqlite-amalgamation to produce sqlite3.o, then link a C tool against it.

Full autotools build of an out-of-tree C plugin with a long exact ./configure flag list and dependency installation.
Configure Ruby with --disable-* feature flags, build miniruby, install the binary and verify it runs.

Compile CPython 3.9.1 from source on Debian and end with a working python3.9 executable installed on the system.

nginx 1.23.2 from source: resolve build deps, configure, make install, and prove the installed binary runs.

VirtualBuildEnv activation/deactivation scripts and their naming; build-environment and PATH-style env setup.
Build environment variables not set correctly for a package build; same class of toolchain env wiring.
CMakeDeps transitive dependency handling; C/C++ build-graph and generated build-config correctness.
Add jobs parameter to generated CMake build presets; touches how the C++ build is actually invoked.
Build-type/config mismatch in generated CMakeDeps files; same territory of build configuration correctness.
Transitive requires produce wrong component linkage; linking semantics of C libraries, shared with the -l/-L work here.
Generated files for a given arch setting are wrong; per-architecture build settings reasoning, weak form match.
CMakeDeps emits bad config for multiple versions of a dep; C/C++ packaging domain only, little build-from-source skill.

SWE-Rebench-Tasks-Clean.reason: Wheel ABI tag wrong for a debug build of CPython; reasoning about how build flags change emitted artifacts.
CMake-driven build backend mishandles config settings that select build options; closest build-configuration bug here.
Wrong executable picked because of PATH resolution order; same PATH-visibility reasoning the verifier checks.
Build failure of a CMake build backend under a distro packaging build; reading a build log back to a cause.
Reorganising the build-option section of a CMake build backend; build-configuration naming only.
PEP517 build-env failure traced through build_meta; debugging an isolated build invocation.
sdist produced by build_meta omits setup.py; packaging-output completeness, adjacent to build/install correctness.
setup_requires must override system versions; resolving build-time dependencies before a build can run.
Python binding over a C library where build/runtime library behaviour leaks through; only loose C-library domain overlap.
Add a pip flag for credential fetching; installation tooling domain but no compilation skill at all.

final_top10.reason: Fix sqlite-autoconf build breakage and run ./configure && make to get a working sqlite3 binary; same package, same build system.
Vendored SQLite source with deliberately disabled build features; repair config and compile sqlite3 with them enabled.
Find the required CFLAGS, rebuild, and verify the resulting instrumentation section exists — the exact crux of the gcov check.
Compile the SQLite amalgamation with a specific compile-time feature enabled by fixing its Makefile.
Build a database engine from a source tarball into a prefix and make its binaries resolve from PATH in a clean shell.
Compile a C program from its source tarball and install it system-wide; same genre and comparable depth.
Fix Makefile.in then ./configure --prefix=/usr/local && make install so the compiled binary is usable from PATH.
Build with a non-default feature set selected through configure flags, then install the binary where PATH finds it.
Rebuild a C tool with debug instrumentation by locating the right Makefile flags and verifying the binary carries it.
Pre-supplied local source archive, no network: build and install a C library system-wide from it.

notes: No task anywhere in the 56k pool mentions gcov, lcov, -fprofile-arcs or coverage instrumentation (searched all five corpora), so the nearest skill is 'build from a vendored source tree with a non-default compiler/configure flag and verify the emitted artifact'. The retriever shortlists were dominated by SQLite *query* tasks (right word, wrong skill) and, for RTS, by an online-CV LaTeX cluster that is pure boilerplate overlap; almost every candidate I kept for RTS and TW came from my own searches, not the shortlist. SWE-Rebench is genuinely weak: it has no C build-from-source tasks at all, only Python packaging/build-backend issues, so ranks 3-10 there are low-confidence filler. SWE-Smith is carried entirely by conan-io/conan (C/C++ build flags and toolchain generation); everything else in that corpus is unrelated pure-Python bug fixing.
